title: ISO 26262-Aligned Functional Safety Verification Framework with Explainable Graph Neural Network
problem: Automotive functional safety verification (ISO 26262) requires exhaustive fault injection analysis; traditional simulation-based approaches are slow and lack interpretability for safety certification.
motivation: GNN-based functional safety verification accelerates fault analysis and provides explainable predictions, enabling efficient ISO 26262 compliance verification.
method: Train a machine learning model (a graph neural network) on experiments where deliberate errors are injected into circuits to see how they spread through the design. The model learns to predict which errors are most dangerous for safety and uses explainable techniques (like graph attention) to show exactly which circuit connections matter for each prediction. Validate the model against standard fault injection benchmarks.
key_novelty: A machine learning model that verifies automotive chip designs meet ISO 26262 safety standards by predicting which circuit errors are dangerous and explaining how those errors would propagate.
contributions: Explainable graph neural network for fault propagation understanding
ISO 26262 compliance framework for automotive hardware
Demonstrated speedup over traditional fault injection simulation
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific automotive benchmarks and certification standards coverage not detailed.
primary_theme: explainable GNN for ISO 26262 automotive functional safety verification
